basis: Lilly judgment on manner of death, taking the ninth-house cusp as the imprisoned churchman's Ascendant: Saturn, lord of that sign, in his fall, long retrograde, and posited in the twelfth (prison, secret enemies) = the man is fallen, imprisoned and without rescue; the Moon separates from Saturn and applies to the Sun near the cusp of the eighth (death) = his light is carried to the house of death; the Sun in a fiery sign applying to an opposition of Mars, dispositor of the bishop — Mars is iron, the sword/axe and violent, judicial bloodshed; Mars in an airy and humane sign points the iron to the neck/head of a man (humane sign, public execution) rather than to disease or a fall; the Moon wanting seven degrees of the body of Mars gives the measure of time, seven units on the month scale of a state prisoner awaiting sentence. Combined testimony: a violent death by edged iron at the hands of authority — beheading — not a natural death in prison.
prediction_text: Archbishop Laud will die a violent death by the sword/axe — beheaded in a public, judicial execution — not die naturally in prison. Mars, dispositor of the aged bishop, opposed by the Sun from a fiery sign and placed in an airy, humane sign, with his significator Saturn fallen, retrograde and in the twelfth (prison), and the Moon applying from Saturn to the Sun at the cusp of the eighth, all speak execution by edged iron upon the neck.
timing: Month scale: the Moon wants seven degrees of the body of Mars — main coordinate about seven months from the figure (window: the months of his imprisonment leading to that term)
